newsitem.title: USA: SC jury considers damages in crash of USAir plane.
newsitem.headline: SC jury considers damages in crash of USAir plane.

text.p: A federal jury began hearing testimony Wednesday on how much money USAir should pay the families of two victims in a Charlotte, N.C., crash in 1994.
The same jury decided last week that USAir, now called US Airways Group Inc., was negligent in the crash of Flight 1016 near Charlotte/Douglas International Airport.
The DC-9 crashed in a violent thunderstorm on July 2, 1994, killing 37 people on board.

Jurors will hear about the lives of two of the victims: Ann Sharkey, a graduate student at the University of South Carolina who was flying to Boston to visit a former roommate, and Freddie Sue Sturkie, a grandmother traveling with her son and grandson to visit relatives in Memphis. Sturkie's grandson was killed; her son survived.
James Orr, the victims' attorney, said the awards would set a benchmark against which other claims against USAir will be settled.
Aviation lawyers say such awards typically average about $1 million per case.
